links.outcome: GP perceived value of explainability visualizations for understanding AI CDSS decisions
links.effect: Explainability was judged crucial, but current XAI visualizations appeared to give limited value to clinicians without technical backgrounds.
links.quote: The workshop discussions revealed that while explainability is crucial for understanding AI decisions, current explainable AI (XAI) visualizations appeared to provide limited value to clinicians without technical backgrounds.

links.outcome: GP-reported effect of training-data transparency on trust and acceptance of AI recommendations
links.effect: Participants suggested that disclosing model training information (data sources and elements) would enhance trust and acceptance of AI-based recommendations.
links.quote: Participants suggested that transparency in model training information, including data sources and elements, combined with clear alignment between model decisions and established clinical research findings and guidelines, would enhance their trust and acceptance of AI-based recommendations.

unlisted_practices: Aligning AI model decisions with established clinical research findings and guidelines to increase clinician trust

screen.reason: Empirical qualitative design workshop with General Practitioners examining factors (like XAI and transparency) affecting trust and acceptance of AI-based CDSS.
